title: What If Every Bear Vanished? The Trees Would Notice First

scenes.text: What if every bear vanished? The first thing to change would be the trees.
Bears catch salmon and often eat only part of it. In one study, they killed about 37 percent of the spawning run.
They carry fish into the forest and leave the rest behind. Most of the nitrogen leaves their bodies as urine.
In an Alaska study, salmon supplied about 16 percent of the nitrogen in spruce needles near the stream. Bears delivered over 80 percent of that.
Take the bears away, and trees beside those streams would lose a major source of fertilizer.
Salmon feed the bears, and bears feed the forest. Pull out one link and the chain goes quiet.

description:
What if every bear vanished?
Bears carry salmon from rivers into forests, and one Alaska study traced about 16 percent of the nitrogen in spruce needles to salmon, delivered mostly by bears.
